samples.summary: The new read-side band is bypassable via the board store, the sibling CRDT path that holds the same verbatim docs blocks
samples.evidence: The change's own rationale (yorkie-slides-store.ts:489-497, docs/design/docs/docs.md) is that a slide text body "passes through no Tree attribute codec", so the guarantee has to live on the read of the CRDT because "nothing stops a collaborator calling doc.update with fontSize: 1e9". Boards store the identical shape and are read by an identical, unbanded parser: `yorkie-board-store.ts:374` (`const blocks = yorkieToPlain<Block[]>(rawData.blocks) ?? []`), `:1319` (withTextElement) and `:1351` (shape text) have no `bandBlockNumerics` call. Board elements are rendered through the slides renderer (`packages/board/src/view/viewport.ts` imports @wafflebase/slides; `packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:239,299` call docs `computeLayout`), so a peer's `doc.update` on a board can store a `type:'table'` block with `columnWidths` of N entries — `computeTableLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/table-layout.ts:153,170-201) allocates a LayoutTableCell per (row, column) pair from `columnWidths.length`, which the board path never caps at MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS — or an `Infinity` rowSpan/padding, for every other viewer of that board. The backend v1 PUT *does* band boards (assertValidBoardBody → assertValidElement → assertValidElementData → assertValidTextBodyBlocks → assertValidSlideBlocks → bandSlideBlockNumerics), so the collaborative path is precisely the writer the PUT band cannot cover.
searchedFor: Grep bandBlockNumerics across repo (only slides store + docs package hits)
Grep computeLayout in packages/slides/src and packages/board/src

samples.summary: `read()` bands slide elements and notes but not `layouts` / `masters`, which are equally peer-writable and feed the same text layout
samples.evidence: `const layouts = (root.layouts ?? []).map((l) => yorkieToPlain<Layout>(l))` (:451) and `const masters = yorkieToPlain<Master[]>(rootAny.masters)` (:458), plus `resolveMaster`/`resolveLayout` at :1289 and :1313, bypass `readElement`, so `bandElementText` / `bandBlockNumerics` never run on them. Both arrays live on the same Yorkie root any collaborator can `doc.update`. A master's `PlaceholderStyle.fontSize` / `lineHeight` is copied straight into real blocks by `seedPlaceholderBlocks` (packages/slides/src/model/placeholder-blocks.ts:30,38) and is used to paint the placeholder hint (`placeholderHint: { style: PlaceholderStyle }`, packages/slides/src/view/canvas/text-renderer.ts:96,122), so a poisoned master reintroduces the unbanded font size the element band just closed. The backend PUT walks layout/master text bodies (assertValidLayout, controller:622-629) and bands them, so again only the collaborative path is unguarded.
searchedFor: Read readElement/bandElementText in the same file

samples.summary: The slides PUT bands a run's `fontSize` but not its inline `image.width`/`image.height`, unlike the shared `bandBlockNumerics` it mirrors
samples.evidence: `normalizeSlideInlines` (controller:1203-1208) bands only `style.fontSize`, while the docs-side equivalent this validator is modelled on also drops an unpaintable image (`bandOneBlock`, packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts: `isPaintableImageSize(image.width, image.height)` → `delete inlineStyle.image`). The rationale given for the whole walk — "an image height is a line height" (numeric-attrs.ts module header; isPaintableImageSize JSDoc) — applies identically, so an authenticated `PUT` persists `image: {width: 1e9, height: 1e9}` verbatim into `writeSlidesRoot`. The frontend read bands it, but every non-frontend reader of the stored deck (the v1 `GET`, which echoes `readSlidesRoot` verbatim, and any CLI/API consumer) receives the out-of-band value the band exists to keep out of storage.
searchedFor: Read normalizeSlideInlines and bandSlideBlockNumerics in the controller
Grep readSlidesRoot / GET handler in the controller

samples.summary: Unbounded recursion over attacker-controlled nesting in the slide-block walk (and in the new `bandBlockNumerics`), while the sibling element walk caps depth at 32 for exactly this hazard
samples.evidence: `assertValidSlideBlocks` → `assertValidTextBodyBlocks` (controller:1135) → `assertValidSlideBlocks` recurses once per nested `tableData.rows[].cells[].blocks[]` level with no depth ceiling, on an authenticated endpoint whose JSON body limit is 25 MB (the ceiling the adjacent `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` at :735 was added for, with the comment "enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack"). Each nesting level costs ~40 bytes of JSON, so a body that `JSON.parse` accepts can still exhaust the validator's stack (RangeError → 500 plus the CPU spent parsing). The newly added `bandBlockNumerics` → `bandOneBlock` → `bandBlockNumerics` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts) has the same shape on the client read path, where the paste sanitizer guards the identical structure with `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts). Low confidence because V8's own JSON parser may fail first on extreme depth.
searchedFor: Read MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH and assertValidElementData in the controller

samples.summary: `sanitizeDocStyles` passes unknown properties inside a known entry through untouched, so a peer-written `stylesJson` can put an `href` under every run in the document
samples.evidence: `sanitizeRegistryInline` (:132-148) spreads the stored entry and removes only `image` and the numerics; every other `InlineStyle` key — including `href` — rides through, and `resolveStyleInline` merges that object as the base layer of every run (`resolveBlockInlines`, packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:160-165). `root.stylesJson` is a single peer-writable LWW string that the v1 PUT never inspects (the function's own JSDoc says so), so one collaborator can make the entire document one hyperlink. The navigation sinks do gate the scheme (`isSafeUrl` before `window.open`, packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1840,2194, and the PDF painter), so this is not a `javascript:`/XSS vector — it is an unvalidated peer-controlled value reaching a navigation sink, and the new sanitizer is the natural place to bound it (e.g. drop `href` from a *named style*, which no writer of the registry produces).

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bounds a single row, not the document, leaving a ~200x page-allocation amplification per peer-written row
samples.evidence: The bound is per row (`if (++fragments >= MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN) fragHeight = remaining;`), and `rowHeights` entries are individually banded to MAX_ROW_HEIGHT = 10000 px (~11 pages each). A table of N rows — cheap for a peer to write, N is not bounded anywhere on the read path — therefore still costs O(11N) pages and `PageLine` allocations, and up to 200N in the content-derived case. That is a large constant-factor amplification from a small write; a whole-document page ceiling (or a cap on rows materialised per table) would bound it, and the current design note states the per-row bound as if it bounded the pass.

verdict.reason: I re-derived the claim independently. Repo-wide grep for `bandBlockNumerics` shows callers only in `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts` (435/502/510/529/2253/2300/2343/2733), plus the docs definition/exports and tests — no board file. The board CRDT path holds the same verbatim docs `Block[]`: `yorkie-board-store.ts:374` materializes `yorkieToPlain<Block[]>(rawData.blocks)` into `data.blocks` unbanded, and the two write bridges (`:1319` withTextElement, `:1344-1353` withShapeText) read/clone the same lists with no normalization. `boardToSlidesDocument` (packages/board/src/model/board.ts:42-74) only wraps `model.elements`; grepping packages/board/src for sanitize/band/clamp yields only a test file; the board revision-preview adapter (snapshot-adapters.ts:61-76) is likewise unbanded. Those blocks do reach the unbounded engine: slides `text-renderer.ts:232-239/295-299` call docs `computeLayout`, and its only pre-pass, `normalizeBlockStyle`, is a plain spread over defaults (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:382-384); `computeLayout` dispatches table blocks to `computeTableLayout` (packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:509-511), which takes `numCols = columnWidths.length` (table-layout.ts:153) and allocates a LayoutTableCell per (row,col) pair (table-layout.ts:170-201) with no MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS cap and no span/padding band. A grep for each individual normalizer across the repo finds them only in docs internals, the docs Tree codec, the docs clipboard sanitizer and the backend v1 controller — never on a board path, so the backend PUT band is indeed the only board-side guard and it cannot cover a peer's direct `doc.update`. I found no counterexample; the gap is real and sits in the untrusted-peer-input lane (a collaborator-supplied `columnWidths` of N entries, `Infinity` rowSpan or padding degrades/hangs every other viewer of that board).

finding.summary: The slides numeric band exists only on the REST PUT; the collaborative Yorkie read path applies none, so a peer bypasses the new gate for the exact threat it documents
finding.evidence: `bandSlideBlockNumerics` / `bandSlideCellNumerics` / the `fontSize` band in `normalizeSlideInlines` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:1027, 1060, 1206) are reachable only from `assertValidSlidesBody`, which the diff's own JSDoc calls "the *only* boundary that can do it" because a slide text body "is persisted verbatim as JSON by `writeSlidesRoot` and read back verbatim — it passes through no codec at all". That premise is what makes the gate bypassable: the normal editing channel is a direct Yorkie write, not the REST endpoint. `hydrateRoot` (packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:283-297) is the only thing that inspects a stored deck on read and does structural repair only (`if (!Array.isArray(blocks)) el.data = { blocks: [] }` at :291-293); no `normalizeFontSize`, `normalizeListLevel`, `normalizeRowHeight`, `normalizeTableSpan` or `parseColumnWidthsAttr` is imported anywhere under packages/slides/src or in the slides store (grep returns only export/pptx/text.ts). Attack: an editor on a shared deck runs a patched client and writes `elements[i].data.blocks[0].inlines[0].style.fontSize = 1e9` — or a docs `tableData` block with 100k `columnWidths` entries — into the deck; every other viewer reads it back through `yorkieToPlain` unfiltered into the shared `computeLayout`/`computeTableLayout`. The added gate covers only API callers, so the hostile-collaborator threat the change states is unmitigated for decks while reading as covered.

verdict.reason: The finding's load-bearing premise — that the collaborative Yorkie read path applies no numeric band, so only the REST PUT is gated — is false. The shared band is `bandBlockNumerics` (packages/docs/src/model/numeric-attrs.ts:293), composing normalizeFontSize, normalizeLineHeight, normalizeListLevel, isPaintableImageSize, normalizeRowHeight, normalizeColumnRatio (with a MAX_TABLE_COLUMNS=256 count cap at :342-349) and normalizeTableSpan, recursing into table-cell blocks at :373. The slides store imports it at packages/frontend/src/app/slides/yorkie-slides-store.ts:65 and applies it on the read path: slide `notes` at :435-437; a text element's `data.blocks` at :529-531 — exactly the claimed `elements[i].data.blocks[0].inlines[0].style.fontSize = 1e9` vector; and shape `data.text.blocks` plus every table cell's `body.blocks` via `bandElementText` (:498-513), invoked unconditionally for all non-text/non-group elements at :608. The `tableData.columnWidths` 100k-entry variant is covered by the same slice+clamp. The reviewer grepped packages/slides/src and read only hydrateRoot (:255-300); the band lives in packages/docs under a wrapper name and is applied in read()/readElement().
